title: Elastic GPU Reservation: credits, SLAs, and contract risk matrix
creator: Asha Kapoor
background: Enterprise customers request predictable monthly GPU commitments but want elastic burst capacity and clear SLA tiers. Existing commitment models (flat reserved GPUs + ad-hoc burst) create billing disputes and operational complexity during large seasonal spikes.
description: Design and validate a packaging and pricing construct for Dedicated capacity that introduces a credit-based burst system, three SLA bands, and a contract playbook mapping customer risk profiles to allowable burst behavior and financial remedies. Deliverables: pricing model spreadsheet, contract clauses, canary pricing experiment plan, and go/no-go decision with legal and sales.
proposals: Proposal A - Commitment + Monthly Burst Credits: customer buys reserved GPU units (monthly commit) and receives a monthly pool of burst credits convertible to GPU-hours; unused credits expire monthly. SLA bands: Bronze (best-effort burst), Silver (guaranteed minimal burst), Gold (guaranteed burst up to X% with fast failover).

Proposal B - Elastic Reservation Curve: customers commit to a baseline (lower cost) and purchase a cushion % of baseline that automatically scales within a soft limit; billing billed at blended rate for cushion usage with weekly reconciliation and true-up. Offers simpler invoicing but less granularity in burst control.

Proposal C - Pay-for-Fallback Model: low baseline reservation with automated fallback to hosted model variants during sustained bursts; lower up-front commitment, higher SLAs tied to fallback reliability. This reduces peak provisioning risk but requires investment in smart routing and monitoring.

Hybrid Recommendation - A + fallback: recommended path is Proposal A as core product with optional Proposal C fallback for highest-risk customers (Gold) to guarantee continuity while minimizing reserved fleet over-provisioning.
decision_record: Consensus leaning to Proposal A + optional fallback (Hybrid). Key rationale: preserves predictability for finance teams, provides clear contract terms for burst behavior, and can be instrumented in the control plane without major serving runtime changes. Pricing mechanics and credit conversion formula to be finalized with revenue ops and legal.

comments: 2026-02-16 - Asha Kapoor: Kickoff notes — aligned on problem statement. Sales raised that lack of explicit burst SLAs has blocked 3 deals in the last quarter. Action: produce a contract appendix sample and quantitative example of credit burn rate.

2026-02-20 - Priya Nair (Eng): Feasibility check — runtime already supports soft limits for autoscaling; primary work is telemetry (per-tenant peak tracking) and enforcement hooks for credit exhaustion. Estimate 3 sprints for ops + 1 spike for cost simulation.
2026-02-25 - Marco Reyes (Design): UX feedback — console needs an explicit 'credit pool' view, per-route allocation, and alerting thresholds. Proposed mockups linked in Confluence.

2026-03-01 - Hannah Lee (Legal): Contract note — must include clear definitions for 'burst', 'sustained burst', and remedies: credit refunds vs service credits. Legal prefers a graduated remedies schedule tied to SLA tier breaches.

2026-03-04 - Sales (internal): Pricing sensitivity — high-enterprise customers prefer predictable blended rates rather than visible per-credit consumption; offer both an 'accounts receivable friendly' invoice option and a usage detail export.

2026-03-07 - Asha Kapoor: Pricing iteration — added a conversion table: 1 burst credit = 1 GPU-hour at baseline SKU; Gold customers get 1.5x conversion for short windows. Documented examples for a 100-GPU baseline with 20% monthly burst pool.

2026-03-09 - Liam Chen (assignee): Pilot plan drafted — target three accounts (two high-risk with seasonal spikes, one steady usage) to run a 30-day pilot with monitoring dashboard and billing reconciliation. PRD, billing templates and contract appendix attached.

2026-03-10 - Feedback round — Engineering requests a hard-limit enforcement mode in addition to soft-limit to protect noisy tenants; Sales requests that hard-limits be opt-in for Bronze/Silver tiers only. Action: specify in playbook.
2026-03-10 - Decision owner note: Prepare final playbook for legal review by 2026-03-12 and coordinate pilot kickoff the week of 2026-03-22.
